n: This chapter steps back in time to before chapter 28. The Philistines assemble their armies at Aphek, while Israel camps by a spring in the Jezreel Valley.

f.g: A gathering point on the coastal plain, north of Philistia.
A town and fertile valley in northern Israel.

n: The Philistine rulers parade their troops by units of hundreds and thousands, and David's men march at the rear with Achish.
The Philistine commanders ask what these Hebrews are doing there. Achish defends David as a loyal defector who has been with him a long time.
The commanders angrily demand that David be sent back. They fear he will switch sides in battle and win back Saul's favor with Philistine heads. Their suspicion is sensible.

f.g: Hebrew satan — an opponent or traitor.

n: They remind Achish of the famous song about David killing tens of thousands — of Philistines!

f.w: Saul slew his thousands, and David his ten thousands

n: Achish calls David and, even swearing by Israel's God, praises his integrity. But the other rulers don't trust him.

f.g: A Philistine king swearing by Israel's God, perhaps out of respect for David.

n: Achish asks David to go home in peace so as not to anger the Philistine lords.
David protests, asking what he has done wrong and why he can't fight against the enemies of “my lord the king.” His words are ambiguous — which king does he mean, Achish or Saul?

f.g: Deliberately ambiguous — it could mean Achish or Saul.

n: Achish says David is as good as an angel of God in his eyes, but the commanders have decided he cannot fight.
Achish tells David to leave at first light with his men. God's providence quietly rescues David from having to fight his own people.

f.g: Probably Saul's former servants who joined David.

n: David and his men leave at dawn for Philistine territory, while the Philistines march to Jezreel. David's dismissal will put him exactly where he is needed in the next chapter.
